name: Patuakhali
tagline: Sagar Kanya, the Daughter of the Sea — Kuakata's long beach where the sun both rises and sets over the Bay, the Rakhine settlers' wells and golden Buddhas, and the 'second Sundarban' at Fatrar Char.

guide.bestTime: October to March — dry, cool weather with calm seas, the best season for Kuakata's beaches and the boat trips to Fatrar Char and Crab Island.
guide.gettingThere: Since the Padma Bridge opened in 2022, direct buses run Dhaka–Kuakata (via Bhanga and Patuakhali, ~6–7 hr). Overnight launches still sail Dhaka–Patuakhali on the rivers, though far fewer than before the bridge. There is no railway, and no operational airport (one near Kuakata is only proposed).
guide.difficulty: Easy along the Kuakata beach front and the temples; moderate for the boat trips west to Fatrar Char and east to Lebur Char and Crab Island, which depend on tide and season.

mustVisit.name: Kuakata Sea Beach
mustVisit.description: The 'Daughter of the Sea' — an 18 km sweep of sand on the Bay of Bengal, and one of the rare beaches anywhere where you can watch both the sunrise and the sunset over the water from the same shore.
mustVisit.history: Kuakata, in Kalapara upazila, has long been a place of pilgrimage and fishing, and is now Bangladesh's second great sea-beach destination after Cox's Bazar. Its nickname, 'Sagar Kanya', means Daughter of the Sea.

practical.hours: Open all day; sunrise and sunset are the highlights

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: ~70 km south of Patuakhali town, Kalapara upazila
howToReach.transport: Direct bus from Dhaka/Patuakhali, or local transport from Kalapara

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool, dry months; be on the sand for both sunrise and sunset
tips: Catch sunrise from the eastern (Gangamati) end and sunset from the west
Swim with care and mind the tides
Motorbikes and tour jeeps run along the sand to the nearby spots

mustVisit.name: Seema Buddhist Vihara & the Rakhine Para
mustVisit.description: The Buddhist temple by the beach — home to a meditating Buddha cast in eight-metal alloy and an old bell — at the heart of the Rakhine settlement whose people first gave Kuakata its name.
mustVisit.history: Rakhine (Arakan-origin) Buddhists settled this coast in the late 18th century, digging the wells that named Kuakata. Their Seema Vihara keeps a large Ashtadhatu (eight-metal) Buddha image, and the Rakhine para around it still weaves cloth and keeps the community's traditions.
mustVisit.bestTime: Daytime; Buddhist festivals for the community at worship
tips: Dress modestly and remove shoes in the shrine
The Rakhine market nearby sells handwoven cloth and local food

mustVisit.name: Misripara Seema Buddha Bihar
mustVisit.description: A Rakhine Buddhist temple a few kilometres east of the beach, known for its great seated Buddha statue — said to be one of the largest Buddha images in the country.
mustVisit.history: Misripara, in Latachapli union of Kalapara, is another centre of the coast's Rakhine Buddhist community; its temple draws visitors for the scale and serenity of its Buddha image.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Misripara, ~4 km east of Kuakata beach
howToReach.transport: Motorbike, auto or jeep from Kuakata

tips: Be respectful and quiet — it is an active temple
Easy to combine with a beach-side ride to the eastern spots

mustVisit.name: Gangamati Reserved Forest
mustVisit.description: The forested eastern end of Kuakata beach — a reserved forest of jhau (casuarina) and a coconut grove where the sand meets the trees, and the best spot for sunrise.
mustVisit.history: The Gangamati reserve shelters the eastern shore, its jhau plantation and coconut grove giving Kuakata a green edge and a quieter, wilder feel away from the main beach front.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Eastern end of Kuakata beach, ~19 km along the sand
howToReach.transport: Motorbike or jeep along the beach from Kuakata

mustVisit.bestTime: Dawn, for sunrise over the sea and forest
tips: Time it for sunrise — this is the eastern viewpoint
Combine with the beach ride to Lebur Char nearby

mustVisit.name: Fatrar Char (The 'Second Sundarban')
mustVisit.description: A protected mangrove forest across the water west of Kuakata — a small, wild echo of the Sundarbans, reached by an hour's boat ride through the channels.
mustVisit.history: Fatrar Char is a mangrove reserve on the western side of Kuakata, rich in the trees and creeks of the tidal forest; locals call it the 'second Sundarban' for its likeness to the great forest to the west.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: West of Kuakata, ~1 hr by engine boat

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool, dry months for comfortable boating
tips: Agree the boat fare and route before setting off
Carry water, sun protection and insect repellent

mustVisit.name: Lebur Char & Crab Island
mustVisit.description: The wild eastern reaches beyond Kuakata — Lebur Char's mangrove edge and, further out, Crab Island (Chor Bijoy), where red crabs scuttle across the sand in their thousands.
mustVisit.history: These chars and islands east of Kuakata are reached along the beach and by speedboat. Crab Island earns its name from the swarms of red crabs that cover the sand, best seen in the cooler, drier months.

practical.hours: Daytime; Crab Island is seasonal (roughly Oct–Mar)

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: East of Kuakata; Lebur Char ~5 km, Crab Island further by speedboat
howToReach.transport: Motorbike/jeep along the beach, then speedboat

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool, dry months for the crabs and calm water
tips: Go at low tide and in season for the red crabs
Combine with sunrise at Gangamati nearby

mustVisit.name: Payra Port
mustVisit.description: Bangladesh's third seaport, on the Ramnabad channel in Kalapara — a modern deep-water harbour that has reshaped the economy of this once-remote coast.
mustVisit.history: Inaugurated in 2013 and operational from 2016, Payra became the country's third seaport after Chattogram and Mongla, handling cargo through a dredged channel to the Bay of Bengal.

practical.hours: A working port — view from public approaches

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Kalapara upazila, on the Ramnabad channel

tips: It is a working port — do not enter restricted areas
Of interest for the scale of the new coastal infrastructure

specialties.name: Kuakata Shutki (Dried Fish)
specialties.description: Through the cool months, Kuakata's 'Shutki Polli' (dried-fish village) sun-dries the day's catch on long racks — loitta (Bombay duck), chapila, churi, shrimp and pomfret — to be cooked into the coast's pungent shutki dishes.
specialties.venue: Kuakata Shutki Polli and local kitchens

specialties.name: Rakhine Cuisine
specialties.description: The Rakhine community's cooking — fish curries heavy with traditional spices, sticky rice and nappi (fermented fish/shrimp paste) — served around the Kuakata Rakhine market.

specialties.name: Rakhine Handloom
specialties.description: The Rakhine women of the Kuakata settlement weave bright cloth on handlooms — sold at the Rakhine market beside the beach.

bucketlist.whereOrHow: West of Kuakata, by engine boat

famousPeople.name: Sohag Gazi
famousPeople.knownFor: Bangladesh national cricketer and off-spinning all-rounder — famously the first player to score a century and take a hat-trick in the same Test match. He rose from Patuakhali, his family's home district.

famousPeople.name: Ratan Lal Chakraborty
famousPeople.knownFor: Historian and academic associated with Patuakhali, known for his work on the social and economic history of Bengal.

didYouKnow: Kuakata is one of very few beaches on Earth where you can watch both the sunrise and the sunset over the sea from the same shore.
The name Kuakata means 'the dug well' — Rakhine settlers dug wells along the shore for fresh water in the late 1700s ('kua' = well).
Kuakata's nickname is 'Sagar Kanya', the Daughter of the Sea.
Payra, in Kalapara upazila, is Bangladesh's third seaport — inaugurated in 2013 and operational from 2016, after Chattogram and Mongla.
West of Kuakata lies Fatrar Char, a protected mangrove forest that locals call the 'second Sundarban'.
